channel.title: Read the Bible: The New Testament in a Year
channel.description:
Looking for a simple and meaningful way to read the Bible every day?

Join Pastor Sean Bailey as he leads you through the New Testament in a year, one chapter at a time. Each short daily episode includes the New Testament read aloud and clearly explained, helping you understand Scripture and apply it to everyday life, no matter where you are in your faith journey.

Before each chapter, you will hear a few key look fors to help you know what to listen for as the Scripture is read. After the reading, each episode includes three clear takeaways designed to help you apply God’s Word to your life in practical and meaningful ways.

This daily Bible reading podcast follows a 260 episode plan that aligns with the weekdays of the year, making it easy to build a consistent habit of reading the Bible. Whether you are driving to work, taking a walk, or spending quiet time with God, each episode offers biblical truth, encouragement, and practical insight to help you grow in your relationship with Jesus.

You do not need a seminary degree or hours of free time. If you want to read the Bible, understand the New Testament, and develop a daily rhythm of Scripture and prayer, this podcast is for you.
channel.itunes:summary:
Looking for a simple, meaningful way to connect with God each day? Join Pastor Sean Bailey on a refreshing journey through the New Testament — one chapter at a time. In just a few minutes a day, you’ll hear the Bible read aloud and explained in a way that’s easy to understand, no matter where you are in your faith journey.
With 260 episodes to match the 260 weekdays in a year, this podcast fits perfectly into your daily routine — whether you’re driving to work, taking a walk, or winding down at night. Each episode brings the truth of God’s Word to life with thoughtful explanation, encouragement, and practical takeaways you can carry with you.
You don’t need a seminary degree or hours of free time — just a willing heart and a few quiet moments. Let this be your daily habit of hope, growth, and a deeper relationship with Jesus.

item.title: 1 John 5. Day 198 - Read the Bible: The New Testament in a Year
item.itunes:title: 1 John 5. Day 198 - Read the Bible: The New Testament in a Year
item.description:
1 John 5. Day 198 - Read the Bible: The New Testament in a Year

Episode Notes:

Today's Scripture: 1 John 5 (CSB) Podcast Homepage: The New Testament in a Year Bible Reading Plan: Navigators Bible Reading Plan Contact Sean: seanbailey1985@gmail.com Follow NTIY on Facebook: facebook.com/newtestamentinayear

In Today's Episode

Faith That Overcomes. Confidence in Eternal Life. Confidence in Prayer.

"And this is the testimony: God has given us eternal life, and this life is in his Son." — 1 John 5:11

First John 5 closes the letter by bringing together faith, obedience, love, and assurance. John says that everyone who believes Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and that faith is what overcomes the world. Our confidence is not found in our own strength, but in the Son of God. John makes the message unmistakably clear: eternal life is found in Jesus Christ. Whoever has the Son has life. Whoever does not have the Son does not have life. John writes so that believers can know, not merely hope, that they have eternal life.

John also gives us confidence in prayer. "If we ask anything according to his will, he hears us." Prayer is not a way of forcing God to follow our plans. It is learning to bring our desires under His will and trusting that He hears us as a loving Father. The chapter ends with a simple but serious command: "Guard yourselves from idols." Anything that takes the place in our hearts that belongs to Christ can become an idol. First John 5 leaves us with a strong foundation: believe in the Son, rest in the eternal life He gives, pray with confidence, and keep Jesus at the center of everything.

item.title: 1 John 4. Day 197 - Read the Bible: The New Testament in a Year
item.itunes:title: 1 John 4. Day 197 - Read the Bible: The New Testament in a Year
item.description:
1 John 4. Day 197 - Read the Bible: The New Testament in a Year

Episode Notes:

Today's Scripture: 1 John 4 (CSB) Podcast Homepage: The New Testament in a Year Bible Reading Plan: Navigators Bible Reading Plan Contact Sean: seanbailey1985@gmail.com Follow NTIY on Facebook: facebook.com/newtestamentinayear

In Today's Episode

Testing the Spirits. God Is Love. Perfect Love Drives Out Fear.

"We love because he first loved us." — 1 John 4:19

First John 4 begins with a call to discernment. John tells believers not to believe every spirit, but to test what they hear because false teachers are in the world. The central question is what they say about Jesus Christ. Truth matters, and not everything that sounds spiritual comes from God. John then reminds us that believers have confidence because "the one who is in you is greater than the one who is in the world." Our security does not come from being clever enough to detect every lie. It comes from belonging to Christ and remaining grounded in the truth He has given us.

John then moves to the heart of the chapter: God is love. We know what love is because God showed it to us by sending His Son so that we might live through Him. His love came first. That means Christian love is never simply a feeling or personality trait. It is a response to the love we have already received from God. John says that perfect love drives out fear and then gives us the simple foundation for everything: "We love because he first loved us." First John 4 reminds us to hold tightly to the truth about Jesus and to let the love of God become visible in the way we treat others.

item.title: 1 John 3. Day 196 - Read the Bible: The New Testament in a Year
item.itunes:title: 1 John 3. Day 196 - Read the Bible: The New Testament in a Year
item.description:
1 John 3. Day 196 - Read the Bible: The New Testament in a Year

 

Episode Notes:

Today's Scripture: 1 John 3 (CSB) Podcast Homepage: The New Testament in a Year Bible Reading Plan: Navigators Bible Reading Plan Contact Sean: seanbailey1985@gmail.com Follow NTIY on Facebook: facebook.com/newtestamentinayear

In Today's Episode

Children of God. A Life Transformed by Christ. Love That Moves Beyond Words.

"See what great love the Father has given us that we should be called God's children—and we are!" — 1 John 3:1

First John 3 opens with a remarkable reminder of our identity in Christ. We are not merely forgiven sinners. We are children of God! And when Christ appears, we will be like Him because we will see Him as He is. That future hope should shape the way we live today. John explains that those who have been born of God cannot remain comfortable in a settled pattern of sin. He is not suggesting that believers never stumble, but that genuine faith produces a changed direction. Jesus came to take away our sins and destroy the works of the devil. Grace does not simply change our standing before God. It changes the way we live.

John then brings everything back to love. He points to the cross as the ultimate definition of love: "He laid down his life for us." If Christ loved us sacrificially, our love for others must become more than words. John challenges believers to respond when they see a brother or sister in need rather than closing their hearts. Love is not merely something we feel or say. It is something we do. First John 3 reminds us that our identity as God's children should be visible in both holiness and love. We do not love others to become children of God. We love because we are His children, and His love is transforming us from the inside out.

item.title: Titus 2. Day 192 - Read the Bible: The New Testament in a Year
item.itunes:title: Titus 2. Day 192 - Read the Bible: The New Testament in a Year
item.description:
Titus 2. Day 192 - Read the Bible: The New Testament in a Year

Episode Notes:

Today's Scripture: Titus 2 (CSB) Podcast Homepage: The New Testament in a Year Bible Reading Plan: Navigators Bible Reading Plan Contact Sean: seanbailey1985@gmail.com Follow NTIY on Facebook: facebook.com/newtestamentinayear

In Today's Episode

Sound Doctrine That Shapes Our Lives. Grace That Trains Us. Living in Hope of Christ's Return.

"For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation for all people, instructing us to deny godlessness and worldly lusts and to live in a sensible, righteous, and godly way in the present age." — Titus 2:11–12

Titus 2 shows us that what we believe should shape the way we live. Paul instructs Titus to teach sound doctrine, then immediately explains what that looks like in everyday relationships. Older men and women are called to model maturity and faithfulness. Younger believers are to grow in self-control, integrity, and good works. Even in difficult circumstances, Christians are called to live in ways that honor God and make the gospel attractive to others. Sound doctrine is not simply information we agree with on Sunday. It should be visible in our attitudes, relationships, decisions, and conduct throughout the week.

Then Paul brings everything back to the foundation of the Christian life: the grace of God. Grace does more than forgive our sins. It teaches us to turn away from ungodliness and live differently. That is an important distinction. We do not pursue holiness to earn salvation. We pursue holiness because God's grace has already come to us through Jesus Christ. The same Savior who gave Himself to redeem us is also working to purify us as a people who belong to Him and are eager to do what is good. Grace does not leave us where it found us. It changes what we love, what we pursue, and how we live.

Paul closes this section by pointing us toward "the blessed hope," the appearing of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ. We live between two great moments: Christ has already appeared to bring salvation, and He will appear again in glory. That future hope should shape our present lives. Titus 2 reminds us that following Jesus is not about merely avoiding what is wrong. It is about becoming people who reflect His goodness while we wait for His return. We have been saved by grace, we are being trained by grace, and we are living in hope of seeing the One who gave Himself for us.

item.title: Luke 4. Day 131 - Read the Bible: The New Testament in a Year
item.itunes:title: Luke 4. Day 131 - Read the Bible: The New Testament in a Year
item.description:
Luke 4. Day 131 - The New Testament in a Year

Episode Notes:

Today's Scripture: Luke 4 (CSB) Podcast Homepage: The New Testament in a Year Bible Reading Plan: Navigators Reading Plan Contact Sean through email here: seanbailey1985@gmail.com NTIY on Facebook: Facebook.com/newtestamentinayear NTIY Website: www.newtestamentinayear.com

Episode Highlights:

The Temptation of Jesus. The Authority of God's Word. The Kingdom of God Proclaimed.

"It is written..." Luke 4:4

Luke 4 marks the beginning of Jesus' public ministry, but before He preaches a sermon or performs a miracle, He is led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil. Where Adam failed in the garden and Israel failed in the wilderness, Jesus remained perfectly faithful. Each temptation was a challenge to satisfy legitimate needs in the wrong way, seek glory without the cross, or question the Father's goodness. Every time, Jesus answered with the authority of God's Word, reminding us that victory over temptation begins with trusting and obeying what God has already said.

After His temptation, Jesus returns to Nazareth and reads from the prophet Isaiah, declaring that the prophecy is fulfilled in Him. He announces that He is the promised Messiah who has come to proclaim good news to the poor, freedom for the captives, recovery of sight for the blind, and liberty for the oppressed. The hometown crowd initially marvels at His words, but when Jesus exposes the unbelief in their hearts, admiration quickly turns into rejection. Luke reminds us that people may admire Jesus from a distance, but following Him requires humble faith and repentance.

The rest of the chapter reveals Christ's unmatched authority. He teaches with authority, commands unclean spirits, heals the sick, and demonstrates His power over the kingdom of darkness. Yet Jesus makes it clear that His primary mission is to proclaim the good news of the Kingdom of God. Luke 4 challenges us to trust God's Word when we face temptation, receive Jesus for who He truly is rather than who we want Him to be, and remember that the same Savior who has authority over sin, Satan, sickness, and death is still calling people to repentance and faith today.

item.description:
James 5. Day 68 - The New Testament in a Year

Episode Notes: 

  • Today's Scripture: James 5(CSB)
  • Podcast Homepage: The New Testament in a Year
  • Bible Reading Plan: Navigators Reading Plan
  • Contact Sean through email here:  seanbailey1985@gmail.com
  • NTIY on Facebook: Facebook.com/newtestamentinayear
  • NTIY Website: www.newtestamentinayear.com

Episode Highlights:

Warning to the Rich.  Patience in Suffering.  The Power of Prayer.  

"Therefore, confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, so that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous person is very powerful in its effect."  James 5:16

 

In this episode of "The New Testament in a Year," we explore James Chapter 5 , focusing on the crucial themes of justice, patience, and the power of prayer. This concluding chapter offers warnings and encouragements, addressing both the wealthy oppressors and the suffering believers. It reminds us of the temporary nature of earthly wealth and underscores the importance of using resources in God-honoring ways, while also highlighting the virtues of patience and steadfastness through trials, drawing inspiration from biblical figures like the prophets and Job.
item.content:encoded:
James 5. Day 68 - The New Testament in a Year

Episode Notes: 

  • Today's Scripture: James 5(CSB)
  • Podcast Homepage: The New Testament in a Year
  • Bible Reading Plan: Navigators Reading Plan
  • Contact Sean through email here:  seanbailey1985@gmail.com
  • NTIY on Facebook: Facebook.com/newtestamentinayear
  • NTIY Website: www.newtestamentinayear.com

Episode Highlights:

Warning to the Rich.  Patience in Suffering.  The Power of Prayer.  

"Therefore, confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, so that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous person is very powerful in its effect."  James 5:16

 

In this episode of "The New Testament in a Year," we explore James Chapter 5 , focusing on the crucial themes of justice, patience, and the power of prayer. This concluding chapter offers warnings and encouragements, addressing both the wealthy oppressors and the suffering believers. It reminds us of the temporary nature of earthly wealth and underscores the importance of using resources in God-honoring ways, while also highlighting the virtues of patience and steadfastness through trials, drawing inspiration from biblical figures like the prophets and Job.

item.title: Bonus Episode – Eighteen Inches from Heaven featuring Brock Baber
item.itunes:title: Bonus Episode – Eighteen Inches from Heaven featuring Brock Baber
item.description:
Bonus Episode – Eighteen Inches from Heaven The New Testament in a Year

Episode Notes:

Today’s episode is a special bonus message from worship leader, Brock Baber.  Brock addresses the quiet danger of complacency that can grow when faith stays in our head but never reaches our heart. He challenges us to examine whether familiarity with truth has replaced obedience.

NTIY Website: www.newtestamentinayear.com

Episode Highlights:

Spiritual Wake-Up. Heart Transformation. Urgent Obedience.

“Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.” Hebrews 3:15

 

This episode serves as a loving but urgent call to the Church. Not simply to know the truth, but to live it. Not to settle for being close to Christ, but to fully surrender to Him. Listen prayerfully and ask the Spirit to search your heart. Is the truth you know truly changing the way you live?
